thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache continuous_batching growth detected on shard set tp-ks-*. Anomalous NCCL stalls observed during shard rebalance. Priority: P1. Pager sent to oncall.

elaine: seeing the same. latency spike + 5xx from dedicated hosts in us-west-2. dashboards -> https://dashboards.redwood.internal/kvcache/continuous (pg: batch_queue_length goes exponential)

sam: tagging eng-runtime and ops-sre. any active rollouts? was there a config change an hour ago?

matt: last automated rollout was a batching tweak at 2457999000 (reduced batch threshold). Not seeing manual deploys since. I suspect a shard-partition skew during the TP handshake that left some GPUs overloaded and others idle.

ana: logs from the failing hosts: ```
ERROR kv_shard: kv_cache_overflow shard=7 entries=13402123 max_allowed=1048576
WARN nccl: allreduce timeout during handshake, peer 3 -> stall
``` 

ops-sre: starting emergency mitigation steps. recommendation: disable continuous batching on affected cluster and force per-request routing to stable small batches. Applying flag now: `REDWOOD_KV_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false` for us-west-2 pool.

elaine: apply command run: ```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/kvcache REDWOOD_KV_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false --all
kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/kvcache
``` 

incident-bot: Action logged. Mitigation: disabled continuous batching in us-west-2. Monitoring for queue drain and error rate drop. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

matt: metrics after toggle (t+3m): avg latency down from 720ms -> 210ms, 5xx rate from 6% -> 1.2%. but one cluster node still showing high KV entries and periodic NCCL timeouts.

sam: tracking down shard assignment. hypothesis: tensor-parallel kv shard hash used `gpu_id % num_shards` but when TP group sizes changed the mapping shifted and some shards ended up owning >2x state.

ana: found the offending code snippet in runtime commit 2445000111: ```
// old: unstable when tp-group changes
shard_id = gpu_id % configured_shards;
// fix: use stable global shard mapping
shard_id = consistent_hash(model_id, sequence_id) % configured_shards;
``` 

eng-runtime: We're prepping a minimal hotfix to use consistent hashing for shard placement and to add a guard to limit per-shard KV entries. Draft patch pushed to branch fix/kvcache-stable-shard (PR 3487).

ops-sre: hotfix PR verified in canary. Plan: 1) apply per-cluster guard to drop excess entries (max_entries=5e6) 2) roll hotfix to canary group 3) ramp to remaining nodes. Rolling canary now.

customer-success: heads-up — we saw impact on ~12 dedicated customers in us-west-2, primarily embedding/streaming flows. Two enterprise customers saw sustained SLA violations for ~22 minutes. We're drafting outreach.

elaine: live mitigation checklist completed so far: disabled continuous batching, restarted kvcache daemonsets, applied max_entries guard. Still waiting on PR rollout across rest of the pool. Current status: partial mitigated. severity -> major.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder: oncall shift ends in 25m. please add runbook notes and watch for rebound after hotfix rollout. Use channel ops-sre for escalation.

sam: prepping handoff note for next oncall: what to watch - batch_queue_length, per-shard entries, NCCL error rate, p95 latency. Runbook commands included.

sam: runbook snippet: ```
# quick triage
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=kvcache -o wide
curl "https://prom.redwood.internal/api/query?metric=batch_queue_length&cluster=us-west-2"
# mitigation toggle
kubectl -n inference set env ds/kvcache REDWOOD_KV_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false --all
``` 

ana: can we throttle new requests from hosted API to dedicated when shard rebalance is ongoing? That would reduce load while we patch.

matt: temporary route: add rate-limit for dedicated pool in router service: `rate_limit_per_tenant=250/s` for the affected region. Ops will deploy now.

ops-sre: rate-limiter applied to dedicated us-west-2 pool. Immediate decrease in inflow. Monitoring.

eng-runtime: hotfix rolled to 40% nodes - no regressions in canary. plan to RAMP to 100% in 12m. will post when complete.

elaine: adding follow-up action items for postmortem: - root cause: non-stable shard mapping + continuous-batching amplification - missing guard in kv-shard sizing - improve CI test for TP group change scenarios - customer communication timeline

customer-success: draft message for impacted customers ready; sending to legal for sign-off. ETA 30m.

eng-runtime: hotfix complete on all nodes at t+38m. Observed: per-shard entries rebalanced, NCCL timeouts cleared, latency stable ~200ms, 5xx < 0.5%.

matt: confirmed. marking incident mitigation as successful. Keeping channel open for postmortem notes.

elaine: handing off to next oncall (sam) for overnight watch. Key monitors & dashboards pinned. Sam, please acknowledge.

sam: acknowledged. I'll watch through night and prep a summary for the postmortem doc in /docs/incidents/kvcache-2468000000.

incident-bot: Incident logged as incident/2468-kvcache-shard-skew. Please file full P1 postmortem within 72 hours. :white_check_mark:

customer-success: Customer outreach sent to impacted customers at t+55m. Initial compensation offers included for enterprise customers. Tracking responses.

ops-sre: closing mitigation actions in tracker. Leaving follow-ups: load test for continuous-batching under TP group churn, add alert for per-shard-entry-ratio > 1.5.

elaine: thanks team. postmortem owners: eng-runtime (root cause), eng-infra (deploy guardrails), devex (CI test). I'll start the doc and assign owners.

eng-runtime: will add the PR/commit refs to the postmortem and include the hotfix diff.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation. Open tasks remain for post-incident work and customer follow-up. :eyes:
